招.meaning: A lonely lighthouse keeper ties a bell to the old <part>anchor</part> on the rocks and rings it at dusk, a <part>call</part> out over the waves. One by one the seals swim over, then a whale, then a lost tugboat. All he does is curl a finger to <kanji>beckon</kanji> them.
招.on: Then he puts on a <sound>show</sound>, juggling fish for his guests.
招.kun: He serves tea in a <sound>mu</sound>g and dries the seals off in a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t.

裂.meaning: Soldiers stand in a perfect <part>rank</part> for inspection, and the general bellows 'Chests out!' They puff up so hard that each tight <part>garment</part> rips down the back, one after another like dominoes. The whole row has <kanji>split</kanji>.
裂.on: The tailor gets a glass of <sound>rets</sound>ina for fixing them all.
裂.kun: Sewing them up takes all night and a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines.

蒸.meaning: A frog builds a sauna in the marsh: <part>hot coals</part> at the bottom, <part>water</part> poured over them, <part>one</part> lily-pad bench and a roof of <part>grass</part>. When his glasses fog up, the job is <part>complete</part>. He sits there grinning in a cloud of <kanji>steam</kanji>.
蒸.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey hops out of its mother's pouch to join him on the bench.
蒸.kun: Soon a <sound>moo</sound>se squeezes in as well and fogs up the whole marsh.

才.meaning: A five-year-old builds a working submarine from a bathtub, a bicycle and an old <part>anchor</part> she found in the shed. It dives, it surfaces, it even makes toast. Scientists queue outside her house. She's a <kanji>genius</kanji>.
才.on: Her fuel is a jug of fizzy <sound>ci</sound>der, poured straight into the tank.

腰.meaning: Under a full <part>moon</part>, a werewolf feels a sudden <part>need</part> to dance. He puts his paws on his hips and wiggles, faster and faster, until his tail spins like a propeller. All that power comes from his <kanji>loins</kanji>.
腰.on: A <sound>yo</sound>-yo swings from his belt as he dances.
腰.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala joins in, wiggling her hips behind a <sound>shi</sound>eld.

漁.meaning: A <part>fish</part> sits on the riverbank in a tiny hat, dangling a worm on a line into the <part>water drops</part> of a rain puddle. It hasn't caught a person yet, but it's patient. Even fish like to go <kanji>fishing</kanji>.
漁.on: Its bait is a le<sound>ggy</sound> <sound>o</sound>ctopus, which grabs the line and tries to reel the fish in instead.
漁.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' it sighs, scavenging the bank for a <sound>sa</sound>rdine: fishing for scraps.

律.meaning: A painter rides the <part>chairlift</part> up the mountain, and every time her chair passes a pole she dabs one stripe on the snow below with a long <part>brush</part>. Dab, swing, dab, swing, all day. By sunset the slope is striped in perfect time: pure <kanji>rhythm</kanji>.
律.on: She keeps a box of <sound>Ritz</sound> crackers on her lap and crunches one per stripe.
